subject: multiple years (not the same) and multiple sites, using boxplot and dotplots? HELP!

messages.author: 7ee17c35c72546b9
messages.subject: multiple years (not the same) and multiple sites, using boxplot and dotplots? HELP!
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to use ggplot to plot four sites, all with different years of data. I can get the dot plots to work, but the boxplots collapse all the years into one boxplot. The code I have been using (the closest I can get) is 

qplot(Year, d13C, data = Hex_4.sites.Littoral, geom="boxplot")+ geom_point() +xlab("") + facet_grid(.~Site, scales="free", space="free") + theme_bw()

 

OR

 

ggplot(Hex_4.sites.Littoral, aes(x=Year, y=d13C))+geom_boxplot() +geom_point()+xlab("")+facet_grid(.~Site, scales="free", space="free") + theme_bw()


I have attached my graphs as well. Any help is appreciated!

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: multiple years (not the same) and multiple sites, using boxplot and dotplots? HELP!
parts:
> I am trying to use ggplot to plot four sites, all with different years
> of data. I can get the dot plots to work, but the boxplots collapse all
> the years into one boxplot.

# Create some data to play with, which I hope
# reflects your problem:
d<-data.frame(year=rep(2005:2008,each=50),
value=rnorm(200),
site=rep(LETTERS[1:4],times=50))

# this shows your problem:
ggplot(d,aes(x=year,y=value))+geom_boxplot()+geom_point()+facet_wrap(~site)

# and this fixes it (by making year a factor instead of a
# continuous variable)
ggplot(d,aes(x=as.factor(year),y=value))+geom_boxplot()+geom_point()+facet_wrap(~site)

If your problem isn't that x should be a factor, then you
will need to provide some data, as well as code, to illustrate it.

Ron.

parts:
Hi:

Using position_jitterdodge(), which is new in version 1.0, should
help. The example is a slight variation on the one from its help page:

dsub <- diamonds[ sample(nrow(diamonds), 1000), ]
dsub$Depth <- cut(dsub$depth, c(50, 60, 70))

ggplot(dsub, aes(x = cut, y = carat, fill = Depth)) +
geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = NA) +
geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(), pch = 21)

Dennis
